faqs.question: What does Cytology - Brush Cytology by conventional method measure?
faqs.answer: The test detects the presence or absence of cancerous cells in the patient sample using the brush cytology technique.

faqs.question: Why is Cytology - Brush Cytology by conventional method Test Done?
faqs.answer: • The test is done to detect cancers which may be asymptomatic or showing minor symptoms which may otherwise be missed. • Useful for the differential diagnosis of certain types of cancers. • More convenient as compared to biopsy.

faqs.question: Who Should Get Cytology - Brush Cytology by conventional method Test Done?
faqs.answer: • Patients with suspected cancer not accounting for immediate biopsy should undergo the brush test for early detection and prompt action.

faqs.question: What to expect during Cytology - Brush Cytology by conventional method test?
faqs.answer: The test requires a patient tissue sample scraping which is be obtained during the endoscopy/bronchoscopy procedure. The cytological examination is performed to detect the presence of cancerous cells.

faqs.question: Are any preparations required for Cytology - Brush Cytology by conventional method test?
What if results are High/ Low?
faqs.answer: Positive result may indicate presence of cancerous cells in the sample. This may aid the diagnosis of cancer. Negative result does not rule out cancer. Further clinical correlation may be required. A biopsy may be required if indicated clinically.

faqs.question: What is Cytology - Brush Cytology by conventional method also known as?
faqs.answer: • Brush cytology test • Cytology test • Conventional cytology by brush test
